title: A nested active take refuses only where the nesting actually re-times it

needles: A transparently nested active take renders exactly like the same comp unnested
Each transformation a nesting can impose refuses the active take it would re-time
One comped child placed twice never reaches the collision its ordinals would cause
rendering bit-identically to the same comp unnested
An active take comp nests by the same predicate, N leaves instead of one

installed_sdk.rationale: NestedActiveTakeUnsupported survives with a tighter guard; no CompileErrorCode member is added or removed and no installed header, entry point or SDK type changes. The narrowing is a judgement inside the lowerer about which documents compile, so claiming an installed-SDK surface would advertise a type that did not change.

offline_timeline_cli.rationale: A transformation-free nested comp now compiles where it previously refused, but no CLI verb authors a track's take lanes or its active selection, and none reports in advance whether a nesting will re-time the comp. An author still discovers the verdict at compile time. Owner: NW-D (P0-40-CONTROLS), which binds the CLI to proposal-safe writers.

offline_timeline_mcp.rationale: The generated Timeline MCP schema carries no operation that authors a comp or selects a take lane, and none that reports whether a nesting transforms its child, so the narrowed refusal is not reachable there. Owner: NW-D (P0-40-CONTROLS).

live_product_control.rationale: Product A live timeline authority is absent for the sequencer generally, so neither the documents that now compile nor the surviving refusal is reachable as a live control. Owner: NW-D, and only where that source is Pulp-owned.

design_time_agent_manifest.rationale: No agent-capability row advertises which nestings a sealed comp survives, so an agent cannot ask before authoring one. Owner: NW-D (P0-40-CONTROLS).
